query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of mechanical properties and residual thermal stresses between samples produced by laser powder bed fusion with optimized process parameters and conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the mechanical properties and residual thermal stresses of the samples produced by laser powder bed fusion with optimized process parameters are not improved compared to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing conditions, the hypothesis is falsified

Many scholars have studied HEAs [,,], but most focus on design principles, metallurgical mechanisms, phase changes, micro-structures, and properties of HEAs manufactured by conventional technologies. Several AM methods have been successfully implemented to fabricate structures with HEAs []. The powder bed fusion (PBF) processes, specifically the selected laser melting (SLM) technique, have been widely adopted []. SLM is a powder-bed additive manufacturing technology, which is also advantageous for producing complex-shaped parts []. During the SLM process, rapid melting and solidification are attributable to short-time interaction between laser energy and metal powder, which facilitates the formation of fine microstructure and improves the mechanical properties of the parts []. Meanwhile, ultra-fast cooling helps prevent the formation of intermetallic compounds and element dissolution. Thus, SLM was recently also used for HEA manufacturing, and some studies on the manufacturing, microstructure, and tensile properties of these alloys have been reported [].
